$comment: The layering contract. tools/check-boundaries.mjs enforces this in CI. Edit deliberately.

packages/core.why: core must run identically on device, in a browser, and in a test with no platform at all.

packages/data.why: data is a query layer, not a view layer. Hooks belong in ui/. `fflate` (deps.md): gunzip for the release files fetchVerified checks (P10), and the regs blobs' inflate (T02) — pure bytes in, bytes out, the same on every platform.

packages/ui.why: hooks run under BOTH renderers. Importing either one forks this package.

packages/map.purpose: One <Map> interface; the per-platform adapters live behind it.
packages/map.why: the ONLY package allowed to know that maplibre-gl and maplibre-react-native differ. react-native is listed because the NATIVE half of this package renders native views; the web half renders a div. That split is the reason this package exists, so both platform imports belong here and nowhere else.

apps/mobile.why: an app that imports a map SDK directly can define its own layers, and the two apps drift apart visually. Go through @app/map. Font loading is listed here on purpose: expo-font is an asset loader, and the app shell is the only layer that may register assets. expo-image-picker is here for the same reason (S1): picking a photo opens the platform's own picker or camera — a platform service the app shell wires and hands down (`src/pickPhoto.native.ts` / `.web.ts`), so @app/ui-native draws the buttons and never names a native module. @app/ui-native NAMES the faces (type.ts) and must not load them, or it would need a platform asset pipeline and stop being drawable by anything else. react-native-gesture-handler is here only for GestureHandlerRootView at the root (G1); the gestures themselves are @app/ui-native's.

packages/ui-native.purpose: Phone components (RN primitives). Shared by the native app AND mobile web.
packages/ui-native.why: (T215) pdf-lib writes the highlight annotation onto the synopsis PDF (`regs/highlightPdf.ts`, pure bytes, runs on web and phone alike); expo-file-system is named in ONE file, `regs/synopsisPdf.native.ts` (the phone half of the .native/.web pair that caches the release's PDF and writes the annotated copy). Must render under react-native AND react-native-web. Touching react-dom breaks the native app; touching a map SDK bypasses @app/map. react-native-svg is allowed HERE and nowhere else: it is a drawing primitive that renders under both, and it is the reason there is no charting library. It is deliberately NOT granted to packages/ui — a hook that could reach for a drawing primitive would start returning elements, and logic would leak into what must stay a purely presentational layer (phone / tablet / desktop are layout classes of these same components, T45). react-native-gesture-handler (G1) is allowed here for the same reason: its GestureDetectors run under both renderers, and they only MEASURE — every threshold and decision is @app/core's (gestures.ts) and every action @app/ui's, so a gesture can never do what its button does not. @react-native-community/netinfo (owner 2026-10-21 late) is named in ONE file, `src/connectivity.native.ts` (the phone half of the connectivity .native/.web pair check-platform holds), loaded lazily so an unlinked module costs only the instant offline switch; `netInfoConnectivity.ts` reads its state and names no module.

packages/data/src/sql/drivers.purpose: The node:sqlite driver (tests and tools) and the release-folder reader over it: the only place in packages/data, beside the release drivers, a database may be named.
packages/data/src/sql/drivers.why: A driver satisfies `Db` — four methods — and nothing above it knows which one it got. That is what lets one query layer serve node:sqlite here (tests and tools), sql.js on the web and expo-sqlite on the phone (the release drivers). `packages/data` itself must never name a database: the moment a query reaches for a driver directly, the other two platforms stop being possible.

packages/data/src/release/drivers.purpose: The release's platform adapters (P11): how a release file is fetched, cached, installed and opened on each platform.
packages/data/src/release/drivers.why: Each adapter is a .native/.web pair (check-platform holds the pair) and the ONLY place the release names a platform module: sql.js and Cache Storage on the web, expo-sqlite and expo-file-system on the phone. The loader, the install/update logic and the release source above it are platform-free, which is what lets a test drive them over an in-memory file system and node:sqlite.

packages/data/src/spots.purpose: The user's own records, and the only writable store in the app.
packages/data/src/spots.why: A spot is the one thing here that cannot be re-downloaded, and it lives in a store of its own because the regulation bundle is replaced wholesale on every update. This layer may name a FILE system (that is its job) and may never touch the bundle's database — the two must not be able to share a file by accident.

$comment2: testOnlyImports are permitted in *.test.ts / *.test.tsx ONLY. Test files are not shipped, but they are still boundary-checked: a test importing react-native into core is the same architectural smell as source doing it. @testing-library/react is here because it is the only way to MOUNT a ui-native component — it renders through react-native-web, which is the mobile-web target. It pulls react-dom, which ui-native source may never touch; that is precisely why it is test-only and not in mayImport.
